summary: The original specification of the File Transfer Protocol (FTP) for moving files between hosts on the ARPANET, written by Abhay Bhushan. Its aims were to promote file sharing, encourage indirect use of remote computers, shield users from differences in file storage, and transfer data reliably. It is designed mainly for use by programs but can be used from a terminal. It was replaced by RFC 542.

plainLanguage.summary: This early FTP specification describes how one ARPANET host can ask another to send or receive a file. It separates the command exchange from the connection that carries file data.

subtitle: An early ARPANET file-transfer design with a command connection and a separate data connection.

tldr.problem: ARPANET hosts used different file storage systems, so users and programs needed a shared way to transfer files and use remote storage.
tldr.mechanism: A user sends FTP commands over a Telnet connection, then the server opens a separate data connection using agreed transfer settings.
tldr.outcome: The unit metadata says RFC 354 was obsoleted by RFC 542 and updated by RFCs 385, 454 and 683; this is an early FTP specification.

sections.title: FTP's Goals and Basic Model
sections.content:
The File Transfer Protocol (FTP) transfers files between hosts on the ARPANET. Its goals are to support file sharing, remote-computer use through programs, differences between host file systems, and reliable and efficient transfer. The protocol is designed mainly for programs but can also be used from a terminal.

FTP uses a full-duplex Telnet connection for commands and replies and a separate data connection for file contents. The Telnet connection must stay open while a transfer is in progress.
sections.plainLanguage: FTP lets programs ask a remote host to send or receive a file. Commands and replies use one connection, while the file data uses another.

sections.title: Data Connections, Types and Modes
sections.content:
The user side listens on a data socket. After a store or retrieve request, the server starts the data connection using the selected socket, byte size, representation type and transfer mode. The default byte size is 8 bits.

The RFC defines ASCII, Image, Local Byte, Print File-ASCII and EBCDIC Print File representations. It also defines Stream, Text, Block and Hasp modes, with ASCII and Stream as the defaults. In Stream mode, closing the data connection marks the end of the file. In Block mode, a header contains a 16-bit byte count and an 8-bit descriptor.
sections.plainLanguage: The two hosts agree how file data is represented and sent. For block mode, each block has a size and a descriptor that can mark ordinary data, an end, suspected errors or a restart point.

sections.title: Commands and Replies
sections.content:
Commands use ASCII and end with carriage return followed by line feed. The user can identify itself with USER and PASS, set transfer options, and request operations such as RETR (retrieve), STOR (store), APPE (append), DELE (delete) and LIST.

The server replies with a three-digit code followed by text. The code is intended for programs, while the text explains the reply to a human user. The first digit groups the response, including success, incomplete information, unsuccessful requests and invalid commands.
sections.plainLanguage: The user sends commands such as retrieve or store. The server responds with a numeric code that a program can interpret and text that a person can read.

sections.title: Restarting a Transfer
sections.content:
The RFC says FTP does not detect bits lost or scrambled during transfer and suggests that this may be handled at the NCP level. It does provide a restart procedure for system failures, but only in Block mode.

The sender places printable marker information in the data stream. The receiver records the corresponding position and returns marker information. After a failure, the user can issue a restart command with a marker and then repeat the file-transfer request.
sections.plainLanguage: Block mode can mark a checkpoint in a transfer. After a system failure, the user can request that the transfer resume from that marker.
